cards.titleZh: 室內裝修行為是否適用法規
cards.titleEn: Determine whether works fall under interior-renovation rules
cards.summary: The regulatory definition covers certain fixed ceiling, internal wall, partition and layout works; excluded examples include wallpaper, furniture placement and some movable elements. Building use and scope affect whether review requirements apply.
checks: Describe building use and location
Identify fixed partitions, ceiling or wall works
Record original floor plans and intended changes
Request qualified professional determination for applicability
questions: Are internal walls or fixed partitions changing?
Does the work affect an escape route or shared facility?
cards.limits: Do not claim every residential decorative change requires the same permit; do not claim any project is automatically exempt.

cards.titleZh: 室內裝修專業資格與查詢
cards.summary: Interior renovation design and construction activities may require relevant registered qualified businesses and professionals; official registry information is available for checking.
checks: Record design and施工 scope
Ask for registration evidence and expiry
Check official registry before contracting
Have authorized reviewer accept qualification evidence
questions: Is the design or construction party properly qualified for this scope?
Has the registration been verified recently?
cards.limits: Never infer a company's registration or staff certification from its name.

cards.titleZh: 室內裝修圖說與審查資料
cards.summary: Articles 23–26 describe required applications, evidence of property rights, existing authorized plans, and location, plan, elevation, section and detail drawings for applicable review procedures.
checks: Track drawing version, author and approving professional
Identify missing rights/plan documents
Preserve approved construction issue
Track fire and material check requirements
questions: Which drawing is legally current for work?
What evidence is missing from the application package?
cards.limits: The demo is a document readiness assistant, not an approval authority.

cards.titleZh: 消防設備與避難安全檢查
cards.summary: Relevant renovation review checks include maintaining fire/escape facilities, fire compartments, and building structural elements. Fire-equipment changes may involve separate fire authority review.
checks: Ask whether exits/escape paths change
Flag partitions and fire doors
Check fire-equipment scope with qualified designer
Record authority sign-off if applicable
questions: Will a proposed layout alter escape or fire-safety systems?
Who must validate a safety-related change?
cards.limits: Never let the Copilot approve fire design or technical compliance.

cards.titleZh: 裝修契約範本與工程範圍
cards.summary: The Ministry of the Interior publishes separate sample contracts for design, renovation construction and combined services. Scope, pricing, payment terms and responsibilities need to be aligned to the selected agreement.
checks: Choose design-only, build-only or combined engagement
Identify work scope and exclusions
Attach pricing revision and drawing issue
Document change-order procedure and acceptance parties
questions: Is this a design retainer or a construction commitment?
Which contract version governs the quotation?
cards.limits: A public model form is not a signed customer contract; legal review required for a real engagement.

cards.titleEn: Avoid incorrect statements about 2026 permit changes
cards.summary: The national authority publicly corrected circulating claims that a newly imposed 2026 rule universally changed the start-work permit procedure; it stated that the discussed contract provisions were then a draft and existing application rules had not changed.
checks: Date-stamp reference guidance
Link the original clarification
Ask professional to verify current rule before work
Avoid blanket permit assertions
questions: Has the client's building/use been checked against current law?
Does a newer enacted rule supersede the cited clarification?
cards.limits: Do not treat an old news article as an evergreen legal certification.

cards.titleEn: Design revisions and approved construction instructions
cards.summary: For regulated works, Article 30 addresses work according to approved drawings and how design changes are handled. The recommended product workflow is to hold draft drawings until reviewed, track downstream impact, and prevent unapproved work instructions.
checks: Show original and revised drawing versions
Flag changed safety/material details
Estimate cost and schedule effects
Hold construction-release until required decisions are recorded
questions: Is this an approved drawing or a draft pricing option?
Must the revised drawing be resubmitted for review?
cards.limits: Resubmission requirements are conditional; professional decision needed.

cards.titleZh: 追加減工程與付款里程碑
cards.titleEn: Change order, scope and payment transparency
cards.summary: The official contract resources and consumer-protection guidance motivate traceable scope, price and revision review. StrideBrain can show original scope, added work, actual verified costs, proposed price and approval state as separate objects.
checks: Never overwrite the originally approved contract price
Link change to scope/drawing revision
Keep contractor/subcontractor cost evidence
Distinguish payable milestones from paid cash
questions: What has the client approved in writing?
Does a supplier quote expire before the planned work?
cards.limits: Workflow recommendation derived from public contract context, not a legally mandated universal change form.

cards.summary: Articles 32–34 cover completion inspection and documents for regulated renovation; the official check form references approved drawings, materials, fire/escape facilities and other checks.
checks: Collect completion photos and authorized drawing issue
Reconcile work against approved plans
Identify required inspection and certificate
Track defects, customer acceptance and warranties as company workflow
questions: What evidence is still missing for regulated completion?
Who is authorized to sign the inspection documents?
cards.limits: Never issue an official completion certificate via StrideBrain.

cards.summary: Article 33 sets conditional pathways based on work characteristics, area, floor, fire compartments and unaffected safety systems. It is not a general DIY exemption.
checks: Collect floor, gross floor area and current use
Record whether life-safety elements change
Identify professional signatories
Route regulatory pathway choice for local expert review
questions: Does the project satisfy every stated eligibility condition?
What does the local building authority require?
cards.limits: Software should flag possible relevance only; not make a binding permit determination.

cards.titleEn: Client plans and personal data handling
cards.summary: Customer personal information and home-related documents need purpose-limited handling and appropriate safeguards under Taiwan personal-data law.
checks: Keep company/customer data inside the proper organization
Restrict drawings with residential addresses
Record consent/purpose where required
Support access, correction and deletion workflows
questions: Can subcontractors see only the documents necessary for their work?
How long should this client's records be retained?
cards.limits: Specific lawful basis and retention duties depend on actual processing and counsel review.

cards.summary: The business-tax law provides the framework for different tax rates and calculation. The demo's flat 5% is an explicit illustrative assumption, not verification of the client company's actual tax obligations.
checks: Keep net price, tax assumption and gross price separate
Label budget, estimate, accepted contract and actual collections distinctly
Owner/accountant verifies tax treatment
Only approved quotes go to customer
questions: Is the estimate tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive?
Is this a proposed price or accepted contract?
cards.limits: No automated legal or tax conclusions.

cards.summary: Prepress planning includes job-ticket preparation, artwork checks, imposition and cost estimates. As a model workflow, collect print size, quantities, stock, colors, finishing and due date before pricing.
checks: Require finished size and run quantity
Capture single/double sided and color details
Select paper/finish/binding
Link promised delivery to job capacity confirmation
questions: Is this a new print run or a reprint?
What quantity, substrate and finishing are required?
cards.limits: Real shop equipment and quoting formulas are company-specific.

cards.summary: A Taiwanese printer publicly lists PDF delivery, recommended image resolution of at least 300 dpi, 3 mm bleed, and embedded/outlined fonts for its poster/postcard products.
checks: Inspect actual file type and dimensions
Check bleed as required by selected vendor
Check placed image resolution
Check embedded fonts or text outlines
questions: Which printer/specification governs this order?
Does the input artwork meet that agreed vendor rule?
cards.limits: These are one printer's published product requirements, not universal legal print standards.

cards.titleEn: A3 trim and 3 mm bleed example
cards.summary: An A3 trimmed poster is shown by one Taiwan provider as 297 × 420 mm, with 303 × 426 mm file dimensions including 3 mm bleed around each edge.
checks: Record trim versus artwork size separately
Compare width/height in millimeters
Flag insufficient bleed for preflight review
Check orientation and safe margins
questions: Is 297 × 420 mm the requested finished size?
Does the press-ready PDF measure 303 × 426 mm if using this 3 mm specification?
cards.limits: Do not apply this rule to books, packaging dies or all commercial prints.

cards.summary: Taiwanese vendor guidance recommends CMYK for color work and grayscale for mono work while explaining that RGB files may still be printed after conversion, potentially with different visual results.
checks: Record color space and desired match tolerance
Offer physical or calibrated proof where appropriate
Explain conversion risks to customer
Preserve customer-approved proof version
questions: Is color accuracy important enough to require a proof?
Is the CMYK recommendation a contractual requirement for this printer?
cards.limits: Do not universally reject RGB files or promise exact color matching.

cards.titleEn: Book cover/interior and binding file practices
cards.summary: A Taiwan printer's book instructions call for separate cover and interior files, PDF settings, binding-dependent cover construction and page arrangement, with distinct examples for saddle stitch and perfect binding.
checks: Capture binding type, spine and page count
Keep cover and interior file versions separate
Check binding-specific imposition and bleed
Record sample proof review before printing
questions: How many pages and which binding type?
Are files split according to the selected print vendor's requirements?
cards.limits: Do not carry a vendor's binding page limits across other presses without verification.

cards.titleEn: Prepress, imposition and job costing concepts
cards.summary: Prepress education in Taiwan explicitly covers file preflight, imposition calculations, job tickets and cost estimation; the demo can expose these concepts as cost lines rather than infer them invisibly.
checks: Identify setup/makeready costs
Separate material, press, finishing and delivery lines
Validate print quantity and layout/imposition
Record scrap and overrun assumptions
questions: What press setup is required?
How many sellable pieces per sheet and what waste allowance applies?
cards.limits: Prices and production speeds must come from the individual company's records.

cards.titleEn: Proofing and approval before a print run
cards.summary: A historic government printing contract illustrates repeated proof review and a full sample approved before final printing. It is a concrete contract example, not a universal law for all jobs.
checks: Track proof version and correction round
Record acceptance of color/trim/sample
Block press-release without required client sign-off
Preserve issued-to-production file checksum or revision
questions: Has the customer approved the correct proof revision?
Does the signed contract require a physical proof?
cards.limits: Do not impose this specific government procurement contract on private commercial customers.

cards.titleEn: Finishing and binding as first-class production stages
cards.summary: The Taipei printing association describes an ecosystem spanning prepress, press and postpress. Published book guidance demonstrates finishing and binding variation. In StrideBrain, finishing should be an explicit task and cost stage.
checks: Define trim, fold, lamination and binding requirements
Connect finish choices to stock and schedule
Inspect defects and tolerance concerns
Allocate finishing vendor owner and due dates
questions: What post-press process is required?
Is an external finishing vendor involved?
cards.limits: This is a workflow model, not a claim every printer owns every machine.

cards.titleZh: 印刷品驗收與重印風險
cards.summary: A public printed-material procurement example specifies output-quality inspection and remedies such as corrections or reprints. The demo should distinguish approved artwork from delivered-product acceptance.
checks: Record sampling/inspection criteria
Link defects to job ticket and proof revision
Flag possible reprint with cost impact
Track delivery and acceptance evidence
questions: Does the delivered job match the approved proof and order?
What do actual contract terms require if print quality is rejected?
cards.limits: Public tender conditions are historic and specific; private remedies depend on actual contract.

cards.titleZh: 油墨、溶劑與空污適用檢核
cards.summary: Printing processes using solvent-based inks, cleansers or coatings may trigger environmental emission control, depending on the regulated process and amounts. Historical environmental correspondence illustrates why ink/solvent usage must be reviewed.
checks: Identify printing process type and relevant materials
Record annual consumption and SDS
Request environmental specialist applicability determination
Track permits and emission-control obligations where required
questions: Does the specific site/process trigger a permit threshold?
What current ministry/local authority rules apply?
cards.limits: Never declare all printers need VOC permits; do not reuse an old letter as current compliance advice.

cards.titleZh: 紙材替代、供應與價格波動
cards.titleEn: Paper substitution and supplier change controls
cards.summary: Print choices affect the prepress output, stock, press setup and finishing. The product should hold a paper substitution until the selected supplier and customer approve material performance, availability, price, and proof implications.
checks: Keep original and proposed stock in change request
Compute direct cost delta separately
Ask for sample proof if color/absorption changes
Create new production ticket only after required approvals
questions: Does the new paper need revised color settings or delivery planning?
Are current supplier costs verified?
cards.limits: Sample workflow design, not a claim of universal stock pricing.

cards.titleZh: 預估與實際印製成本差異
cards.titleEn: Historical estimates versus actual manufacturing cost
cards.summary: Costing should separate estimated materials, setup, printing, finishing, packing and dispatch from actual consumption and accepted outputs so future comparison is defensible.
checks: Record estimated and actual cost codes
Tie reprints/waste to job ID
Do not treat quoted selling price as cost
Review deviations before using history to quote new jobs
questions: Was the job accepted and cost-complete?
Did reprint losses affect actual margins?
cards.limits: The demo's generated cost histories are fictional and cannot prove real market price.

cards.titleZh: 商業報價稅金與客戶資料
cards.summary: Printing quotations and customer contact files need applicable tax treatment and purpose-limited handling of personal data; a sample 5% assumption requires validation for actual trade.
checks: Separate before-tax and inclusive quotations
Protect buyer contacts, shipping information and artwork
Define who sees confidential client orders
Approve outbound communications
questions: Does this company have the correct invoice/tax setup?
Does a contractor need customer personal data for this task?
cards.limits: Company tax situation and lawful purposes cannot be inferred from public examples.

# 室內裝修行為是否適用法規 / Determine whether works fall under interior-renovation rules

Reference ID: REF-I01
Category: LEGAL_SCOPE
Workflow phase: Intake & compliance
Source status: CURATED PUBLIC INDUSTRY REFERENCE (not company-specific)
Last verified: 2026-10-18

## Evidence-based explanation
The regulatory definition covers certain fixed ceiling, internal wall, partition and layout works; excluded examples include wallpaper, furniture placement and some movable elements. Building use and scope affect whether review requirements apply.

## Suggested controls for the StrideBrain demo
- Describe building use and location
- Identify fixed partitions, ceiling or wall works
- Record original floor plans and intended changes
- Request qualified professional determination for applicability

## Questions StrideBrain should ask
- Are internal walls or fixed partitions changing?
- Does the work affect an escape route or shared facility?

## Scope and uncertainty
Do not claim every residential decorative change requires the same permit; do not claim any project is automatically exempt.

- 建築物室內裝修管理辦法 · 現行條文 — Ministry of Justice / Ministry of Interior [Articles 2–3, 9–10, 23–34] (https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?PCode=D0070148)

# 預估與實際印製成本差異 / Historical estimates versus actual manufacturing cost

Reference ID: REF-P12
Category: WORKFLOW_RECOMMENDATION
Workflow phase: Management analytics
Source status: CURATED PUBLIC INDUSTRY REFERENCE (not company-specific)
Last verified: 2026-10-18

## Evidence-based explanation
Costing should separate estimated materials, setup, printing, finishing, packing and dispatch from actual consumption and accepted outputs so future comparison is defensible.

## Suggested controls for the StrideBrain demo
- Record estimated and actual cost codes
- Tie reprints/waste to job ID
- Do not treat quoted selling price as cost
- Review deviations before using history to quote new jobs

## Questions StrideBrain should ask
- Was the job accepted and cost-complete?
- Did reprint losses affect actual margins?

## Scope and uncertainty
The demo's generated cost histories are fictional and cannot prove real market price.

# 商業報價稅金與客戶資料 / Sales tax and personal-data handling

Category: CROSS_INDUSTRY_LAW
Workflow phase: Commercial & privacy
Source status: CURATED PUBLIC INDUSTRY REFERENCE (not company-specific)
Last verified: 2026-10-18

## Evidence-based explanation
Printing quotations and customer contact files need applicable tax treatment and purpose-limited handling of personal data; a sample 5% assumption requires validation for actual trade.

## Suggested controls for the StrideBrain demo
- Separate before-tax and inclusive quotations
- Protect buyer contacts, shipping information and artwork
- Define who sees confidential client orders
- Approve outbound communications

## Questions StrideBrain should ask
- Does this company have the correct invoice/tax setup?
- Does a contractor need customer personal data for this task?

## Scope and uncertainty
Company tax situation and lawful purposes cannot be inferred from public examples.
